newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt ends off with weaker U.S. stocks & bonds.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt ends off with weaker U.S. stocks & bonds.

text.p: Brady prices ended the New York trading session lower Friday, driven by weaker U.S. Treasuries and a sharp drop in stocks.
Peru debt suffered the biggest losses among the latin credits, dealers said.

"We opened this morning with some pretty heavy selling across the board driven by weaker Treasuries and stocks, said one Brady trader. "That drove our market down a little over 10 basis points from yesterday's close."

Another Brady trader echoed the view, noting "We saw four to five waves of selling on the screen in sympathy with Treasury weakness" from dealers who were unwinding long positions prior to the weekend. "However, there's been virtually no customer selling, as a matter of fact they've been buying all day long on the dips."
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond closed off 14/32 at 101-10/32 to yleld 6.52 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 130 points at 7890.
Among the Latin credits, Peru PDIs PEPDI=RR fell one point to 63-3/4 bid, Flirbs PEFLIRB=RR fell 1-1/2 points to a 58 bid, traders said.
"Peru flirbs and pdi's are very illiquid issues, you can send prices down in very little volume, but they too are bouncing back here," said one Brady trader.
On Friday, Peruvian President Fujimori's five new ministers took up their posts following a week of political turmoil, which saw a turbulent cabinet reshuffling and a huge protest march.
Among other Bradys, Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were quoted off 1/8 at 81-3/8 bid, Par bonds BR4D24=RR ended down 1/4 at 70 bid.

"We had a big selloff this morning ... "C" bonds traded as low as 80-5/8 but as the decline in the Bovespa index showed signs of stabilizing ... they're now getting lifted at 81-3/8," said another Brady trader.
Sao Paolo's 47-stock Bovespa index .BVSP dropped over eight percent in early morning trade but later closed off with a 4.66 percent decline at 11182.
The Index had dropped over 15 percent this week in a series of rollar coaster trading sessions.

"Earlier in the week people were focused on the Bovespa," another Brady player said. "Hedge funds that were extremely long watched the market go up ... it doubled basically in seven months and all of a sudden they wanted to all get out at the same time."
"Generally, the market is stabilized here and to some extent I'd argue that we've dislocated it somewhat from the volatility of the Bovespa," he added.
Among other credits, Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR ended off 1/8 at 93-3/4 and Mexico pars MX625L19=RR were off 3/8 79-5/8 bid.
More broadly, Ecuador PDIs ECPDI=RR fell 7/8 to 66-1/2, Bulgaria IABs BGFLTH11=RR fell 3/4 to 74-1/4 and Russian VN US$ RUVNUSLNS=RR was off one point to 92 bid.
